entries.feature: Measuring instruments that keep the semantic payload apart from the encrypted transport: TcpCountRelay (a userspace TCP relay in front of the devbox's SSH port, counting each direction, optional RTT/2 each way, no root or pcap), SruiProbe (the srui subsystem channel over ssh -s, counted as raw bytes and as decoded frames, which must agree; equal to PX-025's DelayRelay count to the byte), TtyProbe (htop's pty stream over ssh -tt), Split (payload never above encrypted; overhead = difference) and nearest-rank distributions; mutants swapping the split or double counting the payload are killed; round 2: the relay counts a byte when it delivers it to the far side, so at an injected RTT the encrypted window no longer leads the payload window by RTT/2 (a read-time-count mutant is killed), and a terminal probe that cannot keep up with htop is killed by a 600 KB drain test

Matched htop comparison: srtop --refresh-interval-ms 1000 against htop -d 10 on a 120x40 pty, alternating, the same idle/busy/churn workloads, 3 s warm-up and 15 s window, 7 runs each; check_matched reads srtop's interval from its published sampling status and htop's from its argument vector in the box and refuses mismatched intervals, windows, terminals or process counts (a -d mutant is killed). Measured: htop's steady encrypted stream was the larger in all three workloads (SRUI/htop medians 0.50, 0.41, 0.48), SRUI's attach was the larger (19-31 KB against 15-19 KB), and SRUI's steady stream grows with the rows that change (6.6 KB/s at 1,000 and 59 KB/s at 10,000 synthetic rows) while htop's is bounded by its screen; no automatic bandwidth superiority is claimed; round 2: htop's terminal size is read back from the session's own stty size (120x40 in every round-2 run) and recorded, so check_matched no longer compares the settings with themselves (a self-comparing mutant is killed)

Latency results: over real SSH at 0/100/300/600 ms RTT (TCP relay), attach medians 724/1677/3461/6195 ms (about nine to ten RTTs, nearly all SSH), steady traffic and commit rate independent of RTT; behind the bridge (PX-025 scenarios, release builds, 3 runs x 10 trials), filter and search results no sooner than the RTT and within RTT + 10.5 ms, and every resume RESUME_OK

The tested envelope and the release notes: R1.md publishes the workload, hardware, build and sampling settings, the measured tables, the process-count/refresh/RTT/bandwidth envelope and the remaining gaps, and says read-only showcase, not htop parity; notes-lint.sh refuses, per clause, claims of parity, equivalence, replacement, superiority, universal smallness and unqualified fewer-bytes comparisons against htop or ncurses, with negation scoped to the claim clause and measured comparisons allowed (round 2: the verifier's survivors and 20 planted claims are caught, 11 allowed statements pass, an Out of scope list is exempt) and runs in selftest.sh; round 3: the lint is documented as a backstop, not a guarantee (the notes' wording is reviewed by a person): it reads paragraphs, negation is the whole words not/no/never/n't only, it targets htop/top/btop/glances/ncurses/terminal monitors, it adds competitive with, faster than, surpasses and reversed comparatives, and only the list under an exact 'Out of scope' heading is exempt; every verifier probe is planted in --self-test

Zero app mutations for an unchanged fake source: over real SSH against srtop --fake-source --smoke-fixture --refresh-interval-ms 100, 0 app transactions and 0 bytes in the 10.0 s after the snapshot, then srtop's SIGUSR1 canary (sent only to the PID ps confirmed) was the next transaction (1 -> 2, two operations); locally at 50 ms the same check passes the frozen source and refuses a changing one; a blind check is killed; round 2: a canary that is not the very next transaction (wrong revisions or operation count) is refused by its own test (the canary-check-ignored mutant is killed)

High-churn delayed range requests make bounded progress: overlapping 16-row CLIENT_MODEL_RANGE_REQUESTs every 250 ms through PX-025's DelayRelay at 100/300/600 ms RTT, against 2,000 synthetic rows churning every 100 ms (all platforms) and live /proc churned by PX-025's short-lived workers (Linux), each converging (a revision committed after it reached srtop, every row held, equal to an undelayed replica's) within RTT + 2 x interval + 750 ms: 12 of 12 at every RTT in every run (max 206/403/702 ms macOS, 209/405/705 ms Linux); a mutant srtop that holds back changed samples is killed as starved or superseded; srtop installs no range provider, so every request is answered AlreadyCached and the test cannot tell an answered request from an ignored one: the generic provider path's progress rests on PX-010-G01's test_model_range_fulfillment_under_concurrent_telemetry (R1.md)
